messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: oncall-db — High severity: DB migration lag + 500s during rollout 'redwood-api v2.3' canary. Affected canary: db-canary-3. Error spike at 18:03 UTC. Paging now. Link: <https://pagerduty.example/incident/12345>

sasha: I'm on page. which migration is this?

oncall-db: It's `20240211_add_user_idx` running as part of the feature rollout. Progress stuck at 0/10 on db-canary-3. CPU fine, but queries queue and we see lock waits.

raj: grabbing logs from db-canary-3, tailing postgres logs now. Suspect ALTER TABLE lock.

raj: ```
2024-02-11 18:02:58 UTC [ERROR] could not obtain lock on relation "users" by executing ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN
DETAIL:  Process 2345 waits for ShareLock on transaction 67890

2024-02-11 18:03:01 UTC [WARNING] pid=2345: canceling statement due to statement timeout
```

marie: if it's a lock on ALTER, we should stop the migration on canary and flip the feature flag to prevent sends to the new path. Killing migration vs waiting — killing preferred to reduce customer impact.

tomas: Agree. Kill the migration on the canary hosts, then `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` if partial index exists. Also set `user_idx_rollout=false` in FF service. If partial DDL committed, we need explicit cleanup.

sasha: executing: `kubectl exec -it deploy/worker-canary -- pkill -f "rails db:migrate"` on canary-3.

incident-bot: Reminder: killing migration can leave partial schema changes. Please verify index/table state and run reverse changes if needed.

raj: Found a partial index: `user_temp_idx` present and in-use by an orphaned transaction. That would block subsequent runs.

sam: I have a rollback script in ops-runbook. Not yet applied. Will prep `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS user_temp_idx;` and verify `schema_migrations` table.

sasha: flipping feature flag now: `/ff toggle user_idx_rollout off` — API reports success, propagation to edge within ~30s. Routing should stop hitting the canary migration path.

marie: after flag flip, switch traffic back to stable for canary group. Also notify CS: some signups may have failed.

customer-success-bot: ALERT: two enterprise customers reported 500s on signup EU region. CS assigned to escalate.

raj: Running cleanup SQL now:
```
-- run on db-canary-3
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS user_temp_idx;
SELECT * FROM schema_migrations WHERE version LIKE '20240211%';
```

oncall-db: `DROP INDEX` succeeded on db-canary-3. `schema_migrations` shows migration '20240211_add_user_idx' as not applied (no row). Good sign.

tomas: Recommend restoring a clean snapshot to canary-3 and re-run migration in a held environment with lock-timeout set. That avoids production-side locking.

sam: Kicking off snapshot restore to canary-1 now, ETA ~12m. I'll coordinate with infra.

sasha: I've rerouted traffic away from canary-3 back to stable pool. 500s dipping back to normal (monitoring shows 95th latency back within baseline).

incident-bot: P0 status: mitigated — migration killed, feature flag toggled off, partial index dropped, traffic restored. Please complete postmortem and follow-ups.

marie: Assigning postmortem owner: raj. Due: EOD tomorrow. Include root cause, why the canary migration acquired locks, suggested safeguards (use `CONCURRENTLY`, add lock timeout, dry-run DDL in shadow DB), and an automated flag kill-switch for future blocking DDL.

raj: Acknowledged. I'll include diffs, timeline, and a runbook for emergency DDL rollback. Also proposing an automatic canary healthcheck that fails the rollout on long lock waits.

sam: I'll open a support ticket for affected customers with a short incident summary and workaround notice.

oncall-db: Closing active page (incident resolved) but leaving thread open for follow-ups and PM notes.

marie: quick action items: 1) add lock-timeout to migrations; 2) add non-blocking index guidance to migrations doc; 3) ensure FF kill endpoint has runbook; 4) add canary DB snapshot test to CI.

sasha: noted. Will add to eng-releases checklist.

sam: Thanks all — good work moving fast and safe. :thumbsup:
